words.prose: {{ar:فِرْعَوْنَ}} ({{tr:firʿawna}}) opens the ayah, but its case-marked appositional shape keeps it dependent on the report of the hosts in 85:17. The most sovereign-looking name is therefore introduced as evidence, not as an actor starting a new scene. Because the word is an opaque foreign proper name, the local force is not Arabic root-play; it is name-recognition. The title-origin and later tyrant-class derivatives stay as provenance, not local derivation: they explain why one base name can summon palace, ruler, court, army, and command-system while remaining a compact item under the prior report-frame. Its recurrence also matters: the name that stands inside prophetic confrontation elsewhere (79:17; 20:24) is here grammatically still, reduced to a remembered case-file. Placed before {{ar:ثَمُودَ}} ({{tr:thamūda}}), it starts the catalogue at ruler scale before the pair widens to collective civilization.

topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence place {{ar:فِرْعَوْنَ}} ({{tr:firʿawna}}) as a foreign proper noun in accusative appositional position, with translation support warning that the pair specifies the prior hosts.

topics.headline: proper name carries ruler-system

topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees how a single recognized name can import the whole imperial apparatus without the ayah narrating that apparatus.
topics.reason: The no-root proper-name analysis keeps the word from becoming Arabic derivation, but the supplied title and derivative evidence supports recognition of the ruler-system compressed in the base name.

topics.reason: The aligned grammar treats the word as a foreign proper noun in case-marked appositional position, matching the CRITICAL claim that form and syntax perform the local reduction.

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) is small, but it does the hinge-work of the ayah. It keeps {{ar:ثَمُودَ}} ({{tr:thamūda}}) coordinated with {{ar:فِرْعَوْنَ}} ({{tr:firʿawna}}) inside the same inherited host-frame, so the second name is not an epithet, afterthought, or new clause. The link is non-hierarchical: two separate exempla become co-witnesses under one warning rather than separate narrative episodes. The same connector also changes the scale of the catalogue at the exact hinge between the names: ruler-power is joined to people-power without adding a verb or explanation. In the written and recited surface {{ar:وَثَمُودَ}} ({{tr:wa-thamūda}}), the letter clings to the second name, making the expansion feel immediate and compressed rather than paused.

topics.headline: coordination keeps shared frame

topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees two separate exempla held inside one warning frame, not a hierarchy or a fresh narrative start.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence strongly licenses {{ar:ثَمُودَ}} ({{tr:thamūda}}) as conjoined with {{ar:فِرْعَوْنَ}} ({{tr:firʿawna}}), preserving both under the prior host category.

topics.reason: The connector stands between the two named exhibits, and the strongly licensed coordination lets the scale shift happen through linkage rather than through a new predicate.

words.prose: {{ar:ثَمُودَ}} ({{tr:thamūda}}) closes the ayah as a coordinated proper name, not as a new sentence. The connector makes it inherit the same appositional role as {{ar:فِرْعَوْنَ}} ({{tr:firʿawna}}), while the proper-name definiteness and fixed recurrence as a name-label let the ayah cite a known people without article or description. Its force is collective: one grammatical item carries a whole civilization, so the pair moves from ruler-centered power to people-scale power and lands on collective collapse. Possible water-root pressure from {{ar:ث م و د}} ({{tr:th-m-w-d}}) remains secondary; the local word is the recognized people-name, not a common water noun or a plural counting individual members. The recurrence field supplies the omitted story: built strength, rock-cut security, denial, and destruction are explicit elsewhere (89:9; 91:11-15), while 85:18 uses only the label. With two bare names, matching dependent shape, final fatḥa cadence, and no predicate, the ayah makes memory do the narrative work, and the final historical denier-name prepares the turn to the present denial category in 85:19.

topics.headline: second name shares dependency

topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the people-name as the second exhibit in the same remembered host-frame, not as a separate clause.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence strongly licenses the word as conjoined with the first name, and QAC marks it as a proper noun in coordinated appositional position.

topics.headline: one name carries a people
topics.summary: The surface is a singular proper name, but its referent is a whole people or civilization.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the warning is not confined to exceptional monarchy; an entire society is compressed into the final name.
topics.reason: QAC identifies a proper noun, while contextual profiles associate the exact form with a disbelieving referent and frequent conjoined behavior.

topics.headline: definite without an article
topics.summary: The proper name supplies an identifiable collective referent without needing an article or description.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes that the ayah relies on a fixed known name-label rather than introducing an indefinite tribe.
topics.reason: The exact proper-noun form is recurrent in the profile evidence, and the local word has no article because proper-name definiteness is already doing the work.

topics.headline: residual-water background subordinated
topics.summary: Possible water-related derivation remains image-pressure only; the local operative value is the proper people-name.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader may feel a faint residue-image behind the name, while keeping the ayah's argument anchored in the recognized people.
topics.reason: The local form is a proper noun and V4 provides no locally activating lexical-sense rows for a common water noun, so derivation is retained only as secondary image-pressure.

topics.headline: family field stays secondary
topics.summary: Cultural and water-related family pressure can accompany the name but cannot turn it into a distributive or common-noun reading.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the people gathered as one civilizational exhibit, not counted as individual members or redefined by etymology.
topics.reason: The ayah uses the collective proper name rather than a nisba plural or common noun, so family evidence is limited to background pressure.

topics.headline: bare name carries remembered indictment
topics.summary: Concrete recurrence references supply built strength, denial, and collapse while the local ayah gives only the name.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader supplies the known story of built strength and denial (89:9; 91:11-15) when the ayah gives only the terse people-name.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows provide concrete references to 89:9 and 91:11-15, and the contextual supplement confirms frequent recurrence of the same proper-name referent.

topics.headline: pair widens to people-power
topics.summary: The second item restricts the host answer to paired exempla while widening the scale from ruler to society.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the catalogue close on collective force, preventing the warning from staying at the level of an exceptional ruler.
topics.reason: The word is the second and final member of the coordinated pair, and attachment evidence preserves the pair's ruler-versus-people contrast.

topics.headline: two names with no predicate
topics.summary: The ayah's bare paired-name architecture and matching final cadence make unlike histories structurally comparable as compact labels.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears two unlike histories compressed into a single paired label-form, so established memory replaces narrated explanation.
topics.reason: The local ayah contains two proper nouns and a connector with no predicate, and the CRITICAL rows identify the shared bare dependent shape and final case-vowel cadence.

topics.headline: scene stripping reaches closure
topics.summary: The final name completes the boundary shift from report-frame to compact content-label.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a whole civilization becomes the closing exhibit under the prior host category, with narrative detail stripped away.
topics.reason: Translation support ties the pair to the prior host-frame, and the final position of the recurrent people-name concentrates the boundary payoff at closure.

topics.headline: history points toward present denial
topics.summary: The final people-name prepares the next ayah's move from historical exempla to a live denial category.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the catalogue preparing 85:19, where remembered deniers become a present category of unbelief and denial.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL row explicitly links the final people-name to the following denial language in 85:19, and the local closing position supports that bridge.

occurrence_evidence_trim.note: TRIMMED, NOT ABSENT. dictionary_entry.occurrence_evidence.occurrences and .ayahs are removed from every root by design: they are a per-occurrence QAC concordance and character-span alignment table carrying zero readings, branches or senses, and they dominated bundle size (~1.5 MB for a single common root). occurrence_evidence.summary (corpus frequency) and .forms (inflectional inventory) are retained. Dictionary/gloss branches are kept in full for every included Furuq root target.

branch_policy.note: No branch filtering is applied. Every branch present in each included dictionary/gloss root entry is kept.

root_mapping.policy: Use the dominant Furuq root for every QAC root, and include non-dominant Furuq targets as additional root_lexicon entries when qac-furuq-v4-root-map marks the QAC root as split.

root_lexicon.note: Turkish is the only language with dictionary entries/glosses currently sourced.
